evidence: Ingested data into Hopsworks feature group leakage_data (v1) and analyzed it on-platform via Trino SQL (delta catalog, table mlpabd5297e_featurestore.leakage_data_1; 800 rows: 286 positives, 514 negatives). Per-class means: f3 = 2.496 for label=1 vs -0.005 for label=0, a separation absent in all other features (f1 0.177 vs 0.022, f2 0.084 vs 0.051, f4 0.142 vs -0.072, f5 0.004 vs -0.011, f6 0.174 vs 0.024). f3 class ranges are completely disjoint: label=1 in [1.990, 2.935], label=0 in [-0.421, 0.457], with tiny within-class stddev (~0.15). A single threshold f3 > 1.0 classifies all 800 rows correctly (100% accuracy). Perfect gap-separated prediction of a binary outcome is the signature of post-outcome leakage, so f3 is the leaking feature.
